newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's biggest labor group scraps May Day march.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's biggest labor group scraps May Day march.

text.p: Mexico's main pro-government labor union will for the third year running skip the annual May 1 Labor Day parade because of fears of political unrest, its leader said on Monday.
Fidel Velazquez, 96-year-old head of the six-million-strong Mexican Workers Confederation (CTM), said the ban was aimed at preventing the march from "turning against the president."
He has called off the parade since President Ernesto Zedillo's government devalued the peso in December 1994, causing Mexico's worst economic crisis in 50 years.

The CTM is one of the central pillars of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) that has ruled Mexico for 68 years. Velazquez, who is fiercely loyal to Zedillo, has run Mexico's pro-government labor unions for half a century, and has no patience for criticism of the PRI.
